claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child or children that you're responsible for? If yes, could you tell me how many children you have and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 years old and lives at home with me. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 16, I need to ask: Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This could include things like:
- School or college (A-levels, BTECs, etc.)
- Certain types of approved training courses

Or has he left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's actually left school recently, but he's just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next. He finished his GCSEs and is in that sort of in-between stage, you know?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's quite a common situation for young people at this age. 

To help determine Alex's eligibility, I need to ask: Has Alex registered for work or benefits with the careers service (or Jobcentre)? And if so, when did he register - what date approximately?

Also, when exactly did he leave education - do you remember roughly when his school or college course ended?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school at the end of the summer term, so that would have been late June. And yes, he registered with the careers service pretty much right after that - it was early July, so just a few weeks after leaving school. He's been working with them to explore his options for what to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing those details. That's helpful information.

Just to clarify - when you say he registered with the careers service in early July, do you know approximately how many weeks it has been since that registration? Is this still fairly recent (within the last few weeks or months)?

Also, I need to confirm: Alex is under 20 years old, correct? (You mentioned he's 16, so just double-checking.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, that's right - he's 16, so definitely under 20. 

As for the careers service registration, it's been about 20 weeks now since he signed up with them. So it's been a few months - time does fly! He's still working with them to sort out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is important information.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Are you the person responsible for Alex - meaning he lives with you and you're responsible for his care and upbringing?
3. Is there anyone else who might also be claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're based here in Manchester. Alex lives at home with me, and I'm responsible for him. And no, there's nobody else claiming Child Benefit for him - it's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the situation carefully based on the rules:

**Key facts:**
- Alex is 16 years old (under 20)
- He left education in late June
- He registered with the careers service in early July
- It has now been approximately 20 weeks since that registration
- You live in the UK, Alex lives with you, and you're responsible for him

**The critical issue here is the 20-week time limit:**

Under UK Child Benefit rules, when a young person aged 16-19 leaves education or training, Child Benefit can continue for a limited "extension period" if they register with the careers service or Jobcentre. However, this extension period is limited to **20 weeks** from the date of registration.

Since Alex registered in early July and it has now been approximately 20 weeks, you are right at the limit of this extension period, or may have just exceeded it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Unfortunately, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

The reason is that while registering with the careers service did allow your Child Benefit to continue temporarily, this extension only lasts for **20 weeks** from the registration date. Since it's now been approximately 20 weeks since Alex registered in early July, that extension period has ended.

**What this means:**
- Your Child Benefit for Alex would have stopped (or is stopping now) at the end of that 20-week period
- To regain eligibility, Alex would need to start approved education or training

**Possible next steps:**
If Alex decides to enroll in college, sixth form, or an approved training course, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. Child Benefit can continue until the child turns 20 (or until the end of the course if earlier) as long as they remain in approved education or training.

I hope this clarifies your situation. If Alex does start a course, you can submit a new claim at that time.

Since it has now been approximately 20 weeks since Alex registered, the extension period has expired or is expiring. Alex is not currently in approved education or training, so Child Benefit eligibility has ended after the 20-week extension period.
